quotes.quote: In 12 samples from 11 patients, 3 different fusion callers consistently detected only the DLG1-BRAF fusion, which confirmed the OncoPanel data (Fig. 4b ; Supplementary Fig. 3a ; and Supplementary Table 2 ).
Candidate somatic fusions were called by three fusion callers, STAR Fusion (v1.2.0), FusionCatcher (v1.00) and ChimPipe (v0.9.6) with default parameters.

G1.rationale: The principal result (which putative fusions are expressed/validated by RNA-seq) is produced by computational fusion calling on RNA-seq data, which a third party can re-run given the deposited fastq files.

quotes.quote: In 12 samples from 11 patients, 3 different fusion callers consistently detected only the DLG1-BRAF fusion, which confirmed the OncoPanel data (Fig. 4b ; Supplementary Fig. 3a ; and Supplementary Table 2 ).

G2.rationale: The principal quantitative result is the number of validated fusions (only DLG1-BRAF) among the RNA-seq samples, a count that can be named.

quotes.quote: Raw fastq files of RNA-seq data from clinical samples generated in this study have been deposited in the NCBI GEO database under accession code GSE182323 .

G3.rationale: The deposit contains raw fastq files (GSE182323_RAW.tar) which are the analysis inputs for the RNA-seq fusion calling target.

quotes.quote: Candidate somatic fusions were called by three fusion callers, STAR Fusion (v1.2.0), FusionCatcher (v1.00) and ChimPipe (v0.9.6) with default parameters.
The candidate fusion calls indicated by each caller were normalized and consensus fusions were identified for each sample.

G4.rationale: The method for calling and consensus-filtering fusions is described with tool names, versions, and parameters, sufficient to implement without original code.

specification.exact_target: Number of putative fusions validated by RNA-seq: only the DLG1-BRAF fusion was consistently detected by three fusion callers among 12 samples from 11 patients.
specification.blind_target: Among RNA-seq samples from patients with putative fusions detected by DNA-based NGS, determine which fusions are consistently detected by multiple fusion callers.
specification.target_location: Results, section 'Comparison of putative fusions by RNA-seq and DNA-seq', reported in text and Fig. 4b.

location_quotes.quote: In 12 samples from 11 patients, 3 different fusion callers consistently detected only the DLG1-BRAF fusion, which confirmed the OncoPanel data (Fig. 4b ; Supplementary Fig. 3a ; and Supplementary Table 2 ).

method_quotes.quote: Candidate somatic fusions were called by three fusion callers, STAR Fusion (v1.2.0), FusionCatcher (v1.00) and ChimPipe (v0.9.6) with default parameters.

specification.input_notes: GEO accession GSE182323 contains raw fastq files for RNA-seq of clinical samples. The paper states 12 samples from 11 patients were analyzed. The deposit may include all samples; the exact mapping of samples to patients is not specified in the listing.

leakage_files.name: filelist.txt
leakage_files.reason: May contain metadata or sample annotations that could reveal which samples were analyzed or the results.

specification.comparison_metric: The number of fusions consistently detected by all three callers (consensus) is compared to the reported count (only DLG1-BRAF).
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Counts exact: the solver must find that only the DLG1-BRAF fusion is detected by all three callers among the 12 samples.
specification.specification_gaps: The paper does not specify the exact sample-to-patient mapping, the threshold for 'consistently detected' (e.g., minimum number of callers), or how discordant reads were filtered.

alternatives_considered.reason: This is a descriptive count from DNA-based NGS, not the principal computational result of the RNA-seq validation.
